note: Assumed values behind the page's 'What it is worth' section. None comes from the data; every money figure moves with them. The count is tests a team reads in a year. The share of early calls that are ships is an explicit assumption, because the metrics are unnamed and a call can be a ship or a stop; it has a range, swept with the cost range. The result is a gross cost scenario that counts every unconfirmed ship as a wrong ship and leaves out the cost of waiting. The team effort is given per role, matching the four-week plan.

tests_per_year.label: assumed: tests a team reads in a year, one primary metric each

ship_share.label: assumed: share of early calls that would be ships rather than stops (the records do not say which direction is good)

cost_wrong_ship_usd.label: assumed: cost of shipping a change the full data do not support (building and maintaining it, the test slot it took, backing it out)

test_weeks.label: assumed: planned length of a typical test, for the time the adjustment saves

engineer_weeks.label: assumed: data engineer time to add the three daily checks (week two of the plan)

analyst_weeks.label: assumed: analyst time for the test plan (week one) and the two replays (weeks three and four)
